candidate.title: Fake "Claim Your SSA Benefits" Retirement Application Phishing Email Scam
candidate.summary: A phishing email disguised as an official Social Security Administration notice urges recipients to "apply" for retirement benefits starting that year, but the embedded link sends victims to a fake SSA look-alike site instead of ssa.gov.
relatedScams: Fake Social Security Statement Email Scam
safetyTips: Never click links in unsolicited emails claiming to be from SSA; go directly to ssa.gov or ssa.gov/myaccount instead
Remember government agencies always use a .gov domain for official email and websites
Delete suspicious emails and do not reply to or call numbers provided in them
Check ssa.gov/scam for current warning signs and to report suspected scam emails to SSA OIG
candidate.howItWorks: Scammers send an email that appears to come from SSA with a subject line like "Claim Benefits!" telling recipients to apply for Social Security retirement benefits. The email's link is disguised to look like SSA's real web addresses, ssa.gov or socialsecurity.gov, but actually redirects anyone who clicks it to a fraudulent website designed to harvest personal information rather than process any real benefits application.
redFlags: Unsolicited email urging you to click a link to "apply" or "claim" Social Security benefits
Link text displays what looks like ssa.gov or socialsecurity.gov but is actually disguised to go elsewhere
Urgent subject lines like "Claim Benefits!" pressuring immediate action
Email arrives from an address that is not a genuine .gov government address
realExamples: SSA OIG reported a scam email with the subject line "Claim Benefits!" stating "Important: Apply for Your Social Security Benefits Starting in 2025," with a link disguised as SSA's official site that redirected to a fraudulent page.
candidate.source: SSA Office of the Inspector General, https://oig.ssa.gov/scam-alerts/2025-07-17-do-not-click-the-link-to-claim-ssa-benefits/

triage.duplicateOf: Fake Social Security Statement Email Scam
triage.reasoning: This is an SSA-branded phishing email impersonation scam, essentially the same category of fraud as the existing 'Fake Social Security Statement Email Scam' and overlapping with 'SSA Imposter Scam Using Real Employee Names and Fake Badges' and 'Social Security Number Suspended Scam' — just a different pretext (retirement benefits application vs. statement), not a structurally distinct mechanism.
